school_name: Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College
title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten verified LSU-area activities requiring neither admission nor a purchase, including campus museums, gardens, art, wildlife viewing, and transit.

cards.title: See Mike at His Campus Habitat
cards.subtitle: Wildlife viewing on North Stadium Drive
cards.notes: Check Mike’s official social accounts before meeting friends there, since maintenance or animal-care needs may keep him inside.
cards.short_summary: Watch LSU’s live tiger from the public viewing area beside the stadium district.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU states that the Tiger Habitat is on North Stadium Drive and that there is no fee to see Mike the Tiger.
cards.access_notes: No fee. Mike is usually outside daily between 8 a.m. and 7 p.m., but times vary; Thursday-morning yard work can delay access.

cards.title: Explore Nine Natural-History Dioramas
cards.subtitle: Free exhibits inside Foster Hall
cards.notes: Meet inside Foster Hall for a self-guided look at the dioramas and interactive displays; contact the museum before bringing a large group.
cards.short_summary: Compare Louisiana wildlife and other natural-history specimens in a compact campus exhibit.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum says its Foster Hall exhibit area, containing nine dioramas and interactive exhibits, is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4 p.m.; large groups should follow the museum’s group-visit instructions.

cards.entity_name: William A. Brookshire LSU Military Museum
cards.title: Trace LSU’s “Ole War Skule” History
cards.subtitle: A free history stop in Memorial Tower
cards.notes: Plan a weekday visit with a friend and use the exhibits to connect LSU’s military origins with the university’s later history.
cards.short_summary: Explore artifacts and stories documenting LSU’s military heritage.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU identifies the William A. Brookshire LSU Military Museum as free and open to the public Monday through Friday.
cards.source_title: Honoring the Past While Committing to the Future
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–3 p.m.

cards.title: Wander Hilltop’s Native-Plant Landscape
cards.subtitle: Fourteen acres of paths, meadow, pond, and woodland
cards.notes: Go during daylight, cross the footbridge, and pause by the meadow or bamboo grove; follow posted rules protecting plants and animals.
cards.short_summary: Take an unhurried walk through a free public arboretum devoted to Southern native plants.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU says Hilltop Arboretum’s grounds are open to the public free of charge seven days a week during daylight hours.
cards.access_notes: Grounds are free and open daily from dawn to dusk. Public restrooms are available Tuesday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

cards.entity_name: Children's Garden at LSU AgCenter Botanic Gardens
cards.title: Look for Butterflies and Edible Plants
cards.subtitle: A no-fee garden walk at Burden
cards.notes: Start in the butterfly garden, read the host-plant labels, then compare the seasonal fruit and vegetable plantings toward the rear.
cards.short_summary: Turn a garden stroll into a group scavenger hunt for caterpillars, butterflies, fruit, and vegetables.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU states that the Children’s Garden is open to the general public seven days a week and that there is no fee to visit.
cards.source_title: Children's Garden | LSU AgCenter Botanic Gardens
cards.access_notes: No fee; open to the general public Monday–Sunday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Teachers planning field trips should register in advance.

cards.entity_name: Trees and Trails at LSU AgCenter Botanic Gardens
cards.title: Walk Three Miles of Burden Woods Trails
cards.subtitle: Woodland paths at the Botanic Gardens
cards.notes: Check in at the Welcome Center, choose a comfortable woodland loop, and keep the paid Windrush Gardens outside this zero-dollar outing.
cards.short_summary: Share a shaded hike through the woods, wetlands, and arboretum portions of Burden.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU describes Trees and Trails as three miles of walking paths, while its visitor handbook states Botanic Gardens admission is free except for Windrush Gardens.
cards.access_notes: Botanic Gardens admission is free except for Windrush Gardens. Current site instructions require all visitors to check in.

cards.entity_name: Alfred C. Glassell Jr. Exhibition Gallery
cards.title: See Contemporary Art at Glassell Gallery
cards.subtitle: Free LSU School of Art exhibitions downtown
cards.notes: Choose a Thursday for the extended public hours, then meet inside the gallery to compare reactions to the current exhibition.
cards.short_summary: View rotating contemporary work presented by LSU’s School of Art without paying admission.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU’s College of Art & Design states that admission to Glassell Gallery and its programs is free and open to all.
cards.source_title: College of Art & Design | Glassell Gallery
cards.access_notes: Free and open to all. The cited LSU page lists Tuesday–Sunday noon–5 p.m., with extended hours to 7 p.m. Thursday and Friday; confirm before travel.

cards.title: Browse LSU Museum of Art for Free
cards.subtitle: Student-ID admission at the Shaw Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Bring a valid student ID for free entry, ride downtown with friends, and check the museum site first for current exhibitions and closures.
cards.short_summary: Spend an afternoon with regional and national art on the fifth floor of the Shaw Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum’s current admission page states that students with ID enter free; it also offers free admission to everyone on each month’s first Sunday.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission — LSU Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Students receive free admission with valid ID. Everyone receives free admission on the first Sunday of each month during museum hours.

cards.title: Take a Free Tiger Trails Loop
cards.subtitle: Campus and nearby neighborhoods by transit
cards.notes: Pick an operating fixed route, meet at an established stop, and ride a loop together; verify the live schedule around holidays and breaks.
cards.short_summary: See more of campus and nearby Baton Rouge from LSU’s fare-free bus network.
cards.evidence_claim: LSU Parking and Transportation says Tiger Trails provides free bus service for students, faculty, staff, and visitors on and off campus.
cards.access_notes: No fare for students, employees, or visitors. Fixed routes generally follow weekday schedules and may be reduced or suspended during breaks and holidays.

cards.entity_name: LSU Museum of Art Free First Sunday
cards.title: Make Art Together on Free First Sunday
cards.subtitle: Monthly no-admission museum day downtown
cards.notes: Schedule the group for the first Sunday, confirm that month’s program online, and use the free-access window without adding a purchase.
cards.short_summary: Pair gallery viewing with the museum’s recurring public free-admission day.
cards.evidence_claim: The LSU Museum of Art states that admission is free for everyone on the first Sunday of every month.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission — LSU Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Free to the public on the first Sunday of every month; the museum lists Sunday hours of 1–5 p.m. Confirm the calendar before visiting.
